key_insight: Independent foundation models for interatomic potentials converge to a common 'platonic' latent geometry, enabling direct cross-model comparison, embedding arithmetic, and diagnostics without requiring ground-truth labels.
problem_solved: Representation incompatibility and lack of label-free tools made it hard to compare, combine, or evaluate different foundation models for interatomic potentials.
method: Extract latent embeddings from multiple independent foundation models trained on interatomic potentials.
Align and analyze these embeddings (geometric/manifold alignment and linear transforms) to reveal a shared 'platonic' geometry across models.
Demonstrate embedding arithmetic and develop ground-truth-free diagnostics to compare and probe model behaviours.
impact: Provides a principled route to interoperable model embeddings, enabling model mixing, transfer, and trustable evaluation without costly reference simulations—accelerating development and deployment of ML interatomic potentials.
visual_elements: Overlay scatter plots of embeddings from different models before and after geometric alignment, showing convergence to a common shape.
Schematic of the 'platonic' latent geometry (simple geometric object) with atom-type/chemistry annotations to illustrate semantic structure.
Illustration of embedding arithmetic (vector operations) that map between chemical motifs or defect states.
Bar/heatmap of ground-truth-free diagnostic scores comparing models across materials/tasks.
paper_title: Platonic representation of foundation machine learning interatomic potentials
